assignedReviews.card_evidence: A person may feel very thirsty, need to pee often, and feel tired when their blood sugar is too high.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe homeostasis as a state of balance among all the body systems in humans that needs to be maintained for survival and proper functioning; its indicators include body temperature, glucose level, and blood pressure
assignedReviews.reason: The card lists symptoms of high blood sugar (thirst, frequent urination, tiredness), which touches on glucose level as an indicator of homeostasis. However, it does not describe homeostasis as a state of balance among body systems, nor does it explain the concept of balance or the other indicators (body temperature, blood pressure). It only provides a symptom of an imbalance, so it is related to the topic but does not directly teach the competency.

copy.en:
What are signs of high blood sugar?

A person may feel very thirsty, need to pee often, and feel tired when their blood sugar is too high.
copy.tl:
Ano ang senyales ng mataas na asukal sa dugo?

Maaaring laging mauhaw, madalas umihi, at mapagod ang tao kapag masyadong mataas ang asukal sa dugo niya.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang senyales sa taas nga asukal sa dugo?

Mahimong kanunay giuhaw, kanunay mangihi, ug kapoyon ang tawo kon sobra ka taas ang asukal sa iyang dugo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: travel really fast at about 300 kilometers per hour
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that how far an object moves in a given time is called speed
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a speed value (300 km/h) for a high-speed train but does not explain that speed is how far an object moves in a given time. It provides an example of speed without teaching the definition or relationship between distance and time, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
How fast do high-speed trains go?

High-speed trains like the Shinkansen travel really fast at about 300 kilometers per hour!
copy.tl:
Gaano kabilis ang mga high-speed na tren?

Ang mga high-speed na tren tulad ng Shinkansen ay tumatakbo nang mabilis, humigit-kumulang 300 kilometro kada oras!
copy.bis:
Unsa ka paspas ang high-speed nga mga tren?

Ang high-speed nga mga tren sama sa Shinkansen modagan og paspas, mga 300 ka kilometro kada oras!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: these 67,000-year-old remains prove ancient humans lived in the Philippines
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how fossils can be used for dating the age of rocks and sediments
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a fossil find and an age (67,000 years) but does not describe how fossils are used for dating rocks and sediments. It provides no explanation of dating methods, relative/absolute dating, or how fossils indicate the age of geological layers. The content is only tangentially related to the competency's core skill.

copy.en: Meet Homo luzonensis! Discovered in Callao Cave in 2019, these 67,000-year-old remains prove ancient humans lived in the Philippines way before Homo sapiens!
copy.tl: Kilalanin ang Homo luzonensis! Natuklasan sa Callao Cave noong 2019, ang 67,000 taong gulang na mga labi ay nagpapatunay na may sinaunang tao sa Pilipinas bago pa dumating ang Homo sapiens!
copy.bis: Kilala ang Homo luzonensis! Nakit-an sa Callao Cave niadtong 2019, ang 67,000 ka tuig ang edad nga mga labi nagpakita nga naay karaang tawo sa Pilipinas sa wala pa moabot ang Homo sapiens!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because it is a homogeneous mixture, meaning every part has the same composition and appearance!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use diagrams and illustrations to describe the arrangement, spacing, and relative motion of the particles in each of the three states (phases) of matter
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the concept of a homogeneous mixture (a solution) but does not address the arrangement, spacing, or relative motion of particles in the three states of matter, nor does it use diagrams or illustrations as required by the competency.

copy.en: A solution is a homogeneous mixture — the dissolved substances are spread so evenly that you cannot see the different parts.
copy.tl: Ang solution ay isang homogeneous mixture — ang mga natunaw na substance ay kumalat nang pantay-pantay kaya hindi mo makikita ang iba't ibang bahagi nito.
copy.bis: Ang solution usa ka homogeneous mixture — ang mga natunaw nga substance nagkatag nga patas kaayo mao nga dili nimo makita ang lain-laing mga parte niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They contain natural sugar!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why fruits and honey taste sweet due to natural sugar, which is about composition and taste, not the physical properties of solid materials (hard, shiny, stretchable) required by G3-M-5.

copy.en:
Why do fruits and honey taste so sweet?

They contain natural sugar! This natural sugar is what makes them taste wonderfully sweet.
copy.tl:
Bakit matamis ang mga prutas at pulot-pukyutan?

May likas na asukal sila! Ang likas na asukal na ito ang nagpapalasa sa kanila ng matamis.
copy.bis:
Nganong tam-is ang mga prutas ug dugos sa putyukan?

Adunay natural nga asukal sila! Kini nga natural nga asukal ang maoy nagpahimuot sa ilang tam-is nga lami.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Honey is much thicker than water! Because it is thicker, it flows more slowly.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume (solids: definite shape and volume; liquids: no definite shape, definite volume; gases: no definite shape or volume)
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses viscosity (thickness) and flow rate of a liquid, but G5-M-3 specifically requires describing properties of solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume. The card does not address shape or volume, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
Why does honey pour so slowly?

Honey is much thicker than water! Because it is thicker, it flows more slowly.
copy.tl:
Bakit mas mabagal dumaloy ang pulot?

Ang pulot ay mas malapot kaysa tubig! Dahil mas malapot ito, mas mabagal dumaloy.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga mas hinay modagayday ang dugos?

Ang dugos mas baga kay sa tubig! Tungod kay mas baga kini, mas hinay modagayday.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Drones are male bees whose only job is to pair with a new queen so the colony can have new bees.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions reproduction in bees, but the competency is about describing the general characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). The card does not describe these characteristics or provide a general statement about living things; it only gives a specific fact about drone bees' mating role. This is a related example, not direct instructional support for the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Drones are male bees whose only job is to pair with a new queen so the colony can have new bees.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: differentiate sexual from asexual reproduction in terms of: a) number of parents involved, and b) similarities of offspring to parents
assignedReviews.reason: The competency requires differentiating sexual from asexual reproduction by number of parents and offspring similarity. The card states that drones pair with a queen to produce new bees, which implies sexual reproduction (two parents), but it does not contrast with asexual reproduction, discuss number of parents explicitly, or address offspring similarity. It is a related fact about sexual reproduction but does not directly teach the differentiation required.

copy.en: Drones are male bees whose only job is to pair with a new queen so the colony can have new bees.
copy.tl: Ang mga drone ay lalaking bubuyog na ang tanging tungkulin ay makipagpares sa bagong reyna para magkaroon ng mga bagong bubuyog.
copy.bis: Ang mga drone mao ang lalaki nga putyukan kansang bugtong buluhaton mao ang pagpares sa bag-ong reyna aron makabaton og bag-ong mga putyukan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A queen honeybee can lay up to about 2,000 eggs — in just a single day!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify which groups of animals reproduce by giving birth to live young, such as mammals, and which reproduce by laying eggs, such as birds and reptiles
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a fact about a bee laying eggs, but does not identify groups of animals that reproduce by giving birth vs. laying eggs, nor does it mention mammals, birds, or reptiles. It only provides a specific egg-laying example without classification.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A queen honeybee can lay up to about 2,000 eggs — in just a single day!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card shows that bees reproduce by laying eggs, which is an example of reproduction, but it does not describe the characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce) as a general concept. It only gives a single reproductive fact without explaining reproduction as a characteristic.

copy.en:
How many eggs can a queen bee lay in a day?

A queen honeybee can lay up to about 2,000 eggs — in just a single day!
copy.tl:
Ilang itlog ang kayang ipangitlog ng reynang bubuyog sa isang araw?

Ang reynang bubuyog ay maaaring mangitlog ng hanggang 2,000 itlog — sa isang araw lang!
copy.bis:
Pila ka itlog ang mahimong ipangitlog sa harianong putyokan sa usa ka adlaw?

Ang harianong putyokan mahimong mangitlog og hangtod 2,000 ka itlog — sa usa lang ka adlaw!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: All the glands in your body that make hormones work together as one team — it's called the endocrine system.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The competency requires describing how the muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory systems work. The card describes the endocrine system, which is not among the listed systems and provides no information about any of the required systems.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: All the glands in your body that make hormones work together as one team — it's called the endocrine system.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models, flow charts, diagrams, and simulations to explain how body systems work together, such as digestion and excretion
assignedReviews.reason: The competency requires using models, flow charts, diagrams, or simulations to explain how body systems work together, such as digestion and excretion. The card only states that glands making hormones work together as the endocrine system; it does not use the required representations nor explain how body systems work together.

copy.en: All the glands in your body that make hormones work together as one team — it's called the endocrine system.
copy.tl: Lahat ng glandula sa katawan mo na gumagawa ng hormone ay magkakasamang nagtatrabaho — tinatawag itong sistemang endocrine.
copy.bis: Ang tanang glandula sa imong lawas nga naghimo og hormone naglihok og tingob — gitawag kining endocrine nga sistema.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Together, they control your whole body.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models, flow charts, diagrams, and simulations to explain how body systems work together, such as digestion and excretion
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that the nervous and endocrine systems work together, but it does not use models, flow charts, diagrams, or simulations as required by the competency, and it does not explain how specific body systems work together such as digestion and excretion.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Your nervous system sends fast electric-like signals, while your endocrine system sends slower but longer-lasting chemical hormones.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the nervous and endocrine systems, which are not among the systems listed in the competency (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory), and it does not describe how any of those listed systems work.

copy.en: Your nervous system sends fast electric-like signals, while your endocrine system sends slower but longer-lasting chemical hormones. Together, they control your whole body.
copy.tl: Ang nervous system ay gumagamit ng mabibilis na senyales na parang kuryente, habang ang endocrine system ay gumagamit ng mabagal pero matagal na kemikal na hormones. Magkasama nilang kinokontrol ang katawan.
copy.bis: Ang nervous system naggamit og paspas nga mga senyales sama sa kuryente, samtang ang endocrine system naggamit og hinay apan dugay nga kemikal nga hormones. Dungan nilang gikontrol ang lawas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A hornet's sting hurts more than a smaller wasp's
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a hornet's painful sting and venom delivery, but does not describe how an animal has changed to better suit its environment, such as mimicry or camouflage. It shares the broad subject of animals but provides no direct support for this adaptation competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A hornet's sting hurts more than a smaller wasp's
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a hornet's sting and size, but does not describe outer body parts such as head, legs, or wings, nor their role in movement or gathering food. It is only tangentially related to animal body features.

copy.en: A hornet's sting hurts more than a smaller wasp's because it's bigger and delivers more venom.
copy.tl: Mas masakit ang kagat ng hornet kaysa karaniwang putakti dahil mas malaki ito at mas marami ang lasong idinideliver.
copy.bis: Mas sakit ang sundot sa hornet kaysa sa gamayng putakti kay mas dako kini ug mas daghan ang gipaambit nga hilo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: horses are used to carry goods and supplies
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a horse but does not describe any outer body parts (head, legs, wings) or their role in movement or food gathering. It only states that horses carry goods, which is unrelated to the competency's focus on body parts and their functions.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: horses are used to carry goods and supplies
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and demonstrate different ways to make objects move by natural causes, such as wind and water, or by people, such as pushing, pulling, rolling, and carrying
assignedReviews.reason: The competency focuses on ways people or natural causes (wind, water) make objects move, including carrying. The card describes horses carrying goods, not people carrying objects, and does not explore or demonstrate movement by natural causes or by people. It shares the word 'carry' but does not directly support the skill.

copy.en: In the provinces, horses are used to carry goods and supplies over long roads.
copy.tl: Sa mga probinsya, ginagamit ang kabayo para magkarga ng paninda at gamit sa malalayong daan.
copy.bis: Sa mga probinsiya, gigamit ang kabayo aron magdala og paninda ug gamit sa layong dalan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A well-cared-for horse can live about 25 to 30 years.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the life cycles of mammals from birth to adulthood, birds from egg to a mature organism, and plants from seed to a young plant, and then to a mature plant
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states a horse's lifespan. It does not describe or compare life cycle stages from birth to adulthood, nor does it address birds or plants. Lifespan is not the same as life cycle stages.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A well-cared-for horse can live about 25 to 30 years.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a living thing (horse) but does not describe characteristics of living things such as growth, response, or reproduction. It only gives a lifespan fact, which is not one of the specified characteristics.

copy.en:
How long can a horse live?

A well-cared-for horse can live about 25 to 30 years.
copy.tl:
Gaano katagal mabubuhay ang kabayo?

Ang kabayo ay maaaring mabuhay nang mga 25 hanggang 30 taon kapag maayos na inaalagaan.
copy.bis:
Unsa kadugay mabuhi ang kabayo?

Ang kabayo mahimong mabuhi og mga 25 ngadto sa 30 ka tuig kung maayong gialagaan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because of hemocyanin — and doctors use it to test vaccines and medicines for dangerous bacterial toxins!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses the blue color of horseshoe crab blood and its biomedical use, with no mention of growth, response, or reproduction—the characteristics required by G3-L-3.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: doctors use it to test vaccines and medicines for dangerous bacterial toxins
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how interaction between living things and interactions between living and non-living things may bring good or harm to the living things involved
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a biomedical use of horseshoe crab blood, which involves an interaction between humans and the crab, but it does not explain how interactions between living things or between living and non-living things bring good or harm to the living things involved. The content is only tangentially related to the competency.

copy.en:
Why is horseshoe crab blood blue?

Because of hemocyanin — and doctors use it to test vaccines and medicines for dangerous bacterial toxins!
copy.tl:
Bakit asul ang dugo ng horseshoe crab?

Dahil sa hemocyanin — ginagamit ito ng mga doktor para suriin kung may mapanganib na bacterial toxin ang mga bakuna at gamot!
copy.bis:
Nganong asul ang dugo sa horseshoe crab?

Tungod sa hemocyanin — gigamit kini sa mga doktor aron sulayan kon adunay peligrosong bacterial toxin ang mga bakuna ug tambal!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: two large eyes on its shell, plus several smaller ones that sense light
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes an outer body part (eyes) of an animal, but the competency requires identifying the role of outer body parts to move and to gather food. The card only mentions light sensing, not movement or food gathering, so it does not directly support the stated skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: two large eyes on its shell, plus several smaller ones that sense light
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about eye structure and light sensing, not about the characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). Light sensing could be a response, but the card does not frame it as a characteristic of living things or teach growth or reproduction.

copy.en:
How many eyes does a horseshoe crab have?

The horseshoe crab has many eyes — two large eyes on its shell, plus several smaller ones that sense light.
copy.tl:
Ilang mata ang horseshoe crab?

Maraming mata ang horseshoe crab — dalawang malalaking mata sa kanyang balat, kasama pa ang iba pang maliliit na nakakaramdam ng liwanag.
copy.bis:
Pila ka mata ang horseshoe crab?

Daghang mata ang horseshoe crab — duha ka dagko nga mata sa iyang kabhang, dugang pa sa uban nga gagmay nga makabati sa kahayag.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They bathe in hot springs to keep their bodies warm
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes animals using hot springs for warmth, but the competency is about identifying basic needs such as air, food, water, and shelter. Warmth is not one of the listed basic needs, and the card does not directly teach any of those needs.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Snow monkeys in cold places like Japan! They bathe in hot springs to keep their bodies warm
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives an example of an animal behavior in a cold environment, but it does not describe a change or adaptation such as mimicry or camouflage. Bathing in hot springs is a behavioral use of the environment, not a described evolutionary change better suiting the animal to its environment.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They bathe in hot springs to keep their bodies warm when snow surrounds them
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe examples and explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet their basic needs
assignedReviews.reason: The card shows animals using an environmental feature (hot springs) for warmth, but the competency focuses on how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet basic needs such as air, food, water, and shelter. Warmth is not presented as a basic need, and no interdependence among living things is shown.

copy.en:
Who else uses hot springs besides humans?

Snow monkeys in cold places like Japan! They bathe in hot springs to keep their bodies warm when snow surrounds them.
copy.tl:
Sino pa ang gumagamit ng hot spring bukod sa tao?

Ang mga snow monkey sa malalamig na lugar tulad ng Japan! Naliligo sila sa mainit na bukal para magpanatili ng init kapag may nyebe.
copy.bis:
Kinsa pa ang naggamit sa hot spring gawas sa tawo?

Ang mga snow monkey sa bugnaw nga dapit sama sa Japan! Maligo sila sa init nga tuburan aron magpabiling init kon niyebe ang palibot.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Does a hot spring mean a volcano is about to erupt?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: Interpret PHIVOLCS Volcano Monitoring (Alert Levels) to demonstrate what to do before, during, and after a volcanic eruption
assignedReviews.reason: The card addresses a misconception about hot springs and eruption warnings, but does not mention PHIVOLCS alert levels, monitoring, or actions before/during/after an eruption. It shares the broad topic of volcanic activity but provides no direct instructional support for interpreting alert levels.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The heat just means there’s hot rock below, not an eruption warning!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use local information or other reliable sources to identify where the nearest active and inactive volcanoes are located and assess the risk of impacts from eruptions to their local community
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not identify locations of active/inactive volcanoes or assess eruption risk to a community. It only clarifies that hot springs are not eruption warnings, which is related to volcanic activity but not to locating volcanoes or risk assessment.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The heat just means there’s hot rock below, not an eruption warning!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not identify local landforms or bodies of water, nor describe how they influence living and non-living components. Hot springs are a type of water feature, but the card does not teach about landforms/water bodies or their environmental influence.

copy.en:
Does a hot spring mean a volcano is about to erupt?

Nope, that’s a misconception! They quietly heat water for thousands of years. The heat just means there’s hot rock below, not an eruption warning!
copy.tl:
Ibig sabihin ba ng hot spring na malapit nang sumabog ang bulkan?

Hindi, maling akala 'yan! Tahimik silang nagpapainit ng tubig sa loob ng libu-libong taon. Ang init ay nagpapakita lang ng mainit na bato sa ilalim, hindi babala ng pagsabog!
copy.bis:
Pasabot ba sa hot spring nga hapit na mosabog ang bulkan?

Dili, sayop na! Hilom silang nag-init sa tubig sulod sa liboan ka tuig. Ang kainit nagpakita ra nga adunay init nga bato sa ilalom, dili pasidaan sa pagbuto!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a gecko only chirps to talk to other geckos
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a gecko's chirp as sound, but it does not explore or describe how sound is made or transferred. It only states the purpose of the chirp (communication), which is not the focus of the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a gecko only chirps to talk to other geckos
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a gecko (a living thing) and its behavior (chirping to communicate), but it does not describe the characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). The chirping is a behavior, not a characteristic like growth or reproduction, and the card does not teach these concepts.

copy.en:
Does a gecko's call really bring luck?

Old Filipino beliefs say geckos bring good luck or signal rain when they call — fun stories! But science says a gecko only chirps to talk to other geckos.
copy.tl:
Totoo bang swerte ang dulot ng tuko?

May lumang paniniwala na nagdadala ng swerte o hudyat ng ulan ang butiki o tuko kapag tumunog — masayang kwento! Pero ayon sa agham, tumutunog lang ito para makipag-usap sa ibang butiki.
copy.bis:
Tinuod ba nga swerte ang gidala sa tuko?

Adunay daan nga pagtuo nga ang butiki o tuko nagdala og swerte o timailhan sa ulan kon motingog — lingaw nga sugilanon! Apan sumala sa siyensya, motingog lang kini aron makigsulti sa ubang butiki.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: house geckos are poisonous
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses a misconception about geckos being poisonous and their harmless bite, but it does not describe outer body parts such as head, legs, or wings, nor their roles in movement or food gathering.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: small, shy animals
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions geckos as small, shy animals but does not describe the characteristics of living things—growing, responding, or reproducing—so it does not directly support this competency.

copy.en:
Are house geckos poisonous?

No! Many people think house geckos are poisonous, but that's not true—they can't really hurt you with a bite. They're just small, shy animals.
copy.tl:
Nakakalason ba ang butiki?

Hindi! Maraming nag-aakalang nakakalason ang butiki, pero hindi ito totoo—hindi ito kayang makasakit nang malala sa tao. Maliit at mahiyaing hayop lang ito.
copy.bis:
Makahilo ba ang butiki?

Dili! Daghan ang nagtuo nga makahilo ang butiki, apan dili kini tinuod—dili gyud kini makapasakit pinaagi sa pagpaak. Gamay ug maulawon nga hayop lang kini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A housefly flies at about 7 kilometers per hour!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that how far an object moves in a given time is called speed
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a speed value (7 km/h) but does not explain that speed is how far an object moves in a given time. It provides an example of speed without teaching the definition or relationship between distance and time, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
How fast does a housefly fly?

A housefly flies at about 7 kilometers per hour!
copy.tl:
Gaano kabilis lumipad ang isang langaw sa bahay?

Ang isang langaw sa bahay ay lumilipad nang humigit-kumulang 7 kilometro kada oras!
copy.bis:
Unsa ka paspas molupad ang usa ka langaw sa balay?

Ang usa ka langaw sa balay molupad og mga 7 ka kilometro kada oras!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Galileo discovered four moons of Jupiter!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions Jupiter and its moons, which are celestial objects, but it does not describe the general structure of the solar system, identify major celestial objects with their features, or discuss composition. It is a historical fact about Galileo's discovery, not instruction on the solar system's structure.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Galileo discovered four moons of Jupiter!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify a famous Filipino and/or foreign scientist and their invention/s
assignedReviews.reason: The card names Galileo as a scientist and mentions his discovery, but it does not identify his invention/s or use information from secondary sources to describe a scientist and their invention. The discovery of moons is an observation, not an invention, so it does not directly support this competency.

copy.en:
How many moons did Galileo discover around Jupiter?

Galileo discovered four moons of Jupiter! That's right, he found exactly four amazing moons.
copy.tl:
Ilang buwan ng Jupiter ang natuklasan ni Galileo?

Apat na buwan ng Jupiter ang natuklasan ni Galileo! Oo, eksaktong apat na buwan ang nahanap niya.

Paano natin nalaman na lumalawak ang universe?

Ang hummingbird! Mao ra kini ang langgam nga makalupad pataas, paubos, ug bisan paatras.

Unsay tawag kon mokunhod og sobra ang kainit sa lawas?

Kung mokunhod og sobra ang kainit sa lawas, mahimo kining makuyaw ug gitawag kini og hypothermia.

Dili, tab-ang nga tubig sila! Naggikan sila sa mga glacier sa yuta nga naporma gikan sa nieve.

Dugay na kining misteryo sa mga siyentista — kung asa gyud mangitlog ang kasili sa lawom nga dagat.

Nganong nagkinahanglan pa og booster shot ang ubang bakuna?

Kay hinay-hinay nga mohuyang ang proteksyon niini, busa ang booster nagpahinumdom sa immune system kon unsaon pagsukol pag-usab.
